uncertain.text: léSanxi, encore viuant: mais pour quel-
uncertain.note: 'lé' and 'Sanxi' are set with no space between them at 6x; transcribed as printed per §1. p004 ends 'vn fils appe-', so the word completed is 'appelé' and the name is 'Sanxi'.

uncertain.text: auoit fait à ſon pere, ſe ſeroit abſentè du
uncertain.note: the accent on the last e of 'abſentè' is a grave: at 7x it is thick at the upper left and thins down to the right, the mirror image of the acute on 'demeuré' in the next line. Read as printed (sic); could be an acute from a damaged sort.

uncertain.text: guſtin, quand il dit, SI TV t'abſtiens longuement ſans la
uncertain.note: the print sets 'S I  T V' as letterspaced capitals, the S full size and I, T, V as small capitals; closed up to 'SI TV' per §3 and the block flagged spaced_caps. The V is the small-capital sort, not a lowercase v.

uncertain.text: & ſi elle mal-verſe, ſon peché ſera reputé à tõ abſtinẽce {a}.
uncertain.note: the word-division sign in 'mal-verſe' is printed as a raised medial point with space on both sides (mal · verſe), not a baseline hyphen and not a period; transcribed as '-' per the §2 table. 'mal·verſe' would be the literal alternative.

uncertain.text: Dont quelques vns ont biẽ oſé dire, qu vn Iuge pourroit
uncertain.note: 'qu vn' is printed with a space and no apostrophe (sic); at 4x the only mark between qu and vn is a speck well above the baseline, far smaller than the apostrophes of 'n'eſt' and 'qu'apres' on this page.

uncertain.text: dehors, ne la peut repudier, par ce (dit Iuſtinien) que luy
uncertain.note: the print sets 'ce(dit' with no space before the parenthesis; spaced per the §1 parenthesis rule.

uncertain.text: bon, que la femme (de laquelle le mari à demeuré
uncertain.note: the print sets '( de laquelle' with a space inside the parenthesis and '(' is widely spaced from 'femme'; closed per the §1 parenthesis rule. Same on the next line, where 'abſent)ſe' is set tight.
the mark after the S dips below the baseline and could be a comma rather than a period; either way the spacing rule prints it the same.
'duquel' and 'ſont' are set with no space between them at 5x; transcribed as printed per §1.

at 9x the numeral shows three minims after the v (dot over the first, the last descending), so 'xxviij'; at reading size it looks like 'xxvij'. A short bar sits over the final ij, apparently part of the ij sort.
'de' and 'Ra' are set with no space between them (the a is pushed up against the R at the line end); transcribed as printed. The note is Petrus Ravennas, 'Alphabetum'.
a separate round dot is printed well to the right of 'Alphabet.' at the same height as the period; taken as stray type and not transcribed.

doubtful. At 10x the line reads: key c, a period, then a word of three letters (round letter with a crossbar + long ſ + the curly italic t) = 'eſt', then 'tabuſtines' (t a b u ſt i n e s). The reading makes no sense as a citation; note a on the same page cites 'c. ſi tu abſti-nes xxviij. q. ij.', so this may be a second setting of the same incipit ('c. ſi tu abſtines'), with the letters I read as 'eſt ta-bu' actually being 'ſi tu ab-'. A small raised tick sits above and right of the key c. Needs a second eye.

the letter between the two numerals has no descender, so it is 'c', not the 'q' that a Decretum citation (and note a's 'xxviij. q.') would want; transcribed as printed. The numeral shows only two minims after the v, so 'xxvij', against note a's 'xxviij'.

'nouuelles' and 'de' are set with no space (as printed). The two letters hanging at the right edge of the line are read as 'Iu' (completing 'Iuſtiniẽ' on the next line); at 9x the I is a short faint stroke joined to the u and only the u is certain.

the l of 'la' is printed as a straight stroke with top and bottom serifs, like a capital I, not the looped italic l used in 'collation' and 'lis'; read as 'la' from the sense ('ſous la collation'). The a sits lower than the stroke, at the extreme right edge of the column.

the character after the v is a tall straight ascender with a small left nub; read as long ſ, but it could be the same I/l sort as in the line above, or a swash i, which would give the Authenticum collation number. A short dash is printed after the period at the line end with nothing following it; taken as stray type and not transcribed.

a hyphen is printed at the line end although 'Conſenſu' is a complete word and the next line begins 'para.'; transcribed as printed. It sits at the same height as the genuine hyphen of 'contige-' in note d.
a period is printed after 'quo' at the line end, although the word continues as 'que.' on the next line ('vir quoque'); transcribed as printed. 'vir' is set in lowercase italic, not as 'Vir'.
the last letter is a round bowl that reads as 'a' rather than the 'o' of 'ergo' in note d, so 'erga'; the mark after it is a heavy blot that may be a period or ink. Reading not certain.
